messages:
Grace Kim: seeing a canary regression on A10 when v2 selector enabled. p95 decode latency up ~18–25% but only for long-context prompts (looks like 8k+ effective ctx). anyone else looking?

Omar El-Sayed: yup, I just got pinged from perf-canary. It’s only the us-east canary cohort (5%) and only A10 nodes. L4/A100 look flat.

Grace Kim: link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/runtime-serving/latency?var-region=us-east&var-gpu=A10&var-selector=v2&from=now-6h&to=now (panel “decode p95 by gpu”) — step change right after canary config landed.

[grafana-bot]: Alert: runtime-serving / Decode p95 (A10, selector=v2) breached threshold (p95 > 410ms for 10m). Runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/selector-v2-rollout-slo-guardrails

Yuki Sato: pulling node inventory now. quick q: are these A10G (AWS) or on-prem A10? SKU normalization might be mapping these incorrectly.

Omar El-Sayed: AWS A10G in us-east-1. Instance type is g5.2xlarge mostly.

Sana Farid: can confirm it correlates w/ long prompts. I filtered traces by request_ctx.effective_prompt_tokens > 6000 and selector=v2, only A10 shows the tail. sample honeycomb query: https://honeycomb.redwood.ai/datasets/runtime/queries/selv2-a10-longctx

Grace Kim: do we see kernel_choice different from v1? maybe v2 is selecting the “fast” long-context kernel that’s actually worse on A10.

Sana Farid: in traces, kernel_choice_id is mostly `attn_flash_v3_long` on A10 + longctx. For A100/H100, same kernel_id but no regression.

Yuki Sato: `attn_flash_v3_long` is gated by sm80+ in my head… A10 is sm86 so it qualifies, but perf characteristics differ (shared mem pressure). there was a note about A10 preferring `attn_xformers_v2_long` beyond some seq boundary.

Grace Kim: our selection matrix for v2 has a special-case for L4 long bucket, but I don’t remember an A10 long override. Might be defaulting to the generic “sm80+ long” row.

Omar El-Sayed: also: the spike is decode-heavy. prefill p95 is basically unchanged.

Lena Fischer: could this be seq bucket boundary mismatch? scheduler is emitting “long” bucket more often than before? i.e. effective ctx calc inflated -> we route into long kernel too early.

Grace Kim: good call. if we’re prematurely classifying as long, A10 might get the worse kernel for mid-length cases.

Marcus Reed: I can reproduce locally-ish on the A10 runner in benchmark-lab. When I run 4k prompts, v2 sometimes labels them long bucket (??). That would explain the surface area.

Marcus Reed: command + output snippet:
```
benchctl run --gpu A10 --model llama-3-8b --dist mixed_long --selector v2
...
seq_bucket=decode_long  (expected decode_med)
...
```

Grace Kim: ok, that smells like an off-by-one / rounding issue on bucket boundaries. Lena, is the scheduler signal “effective_context” including the just-generated token? (decode step adds 1).

Lena Fischer: scheduler side: effective_ctx = prompt_len + generated_so_far + 1 (for next token position). we did that intentionally for kv indexing. but the selector bucket logic might be treating boundary as inclusive on both ends.

Omar El-Sayed: I’ll pull the bucket code path. If it’s `>= 4096` -> long, and scheduler already adds +1, then 4095 prompts become long at first decode.

Grace Kim: that aligns with “4k prompts sometimes long”. depending on exact rounding, 4096 boundary gets hit.

Allison Grant: reminder: if we’re going to hot-adjust bucketing, pls keep telemetry cardinality stable. don’t add new labels in the middle of this incident. :pray:

Yuki Sato: in parallel, I can propose an A10 long override to use `attn_xformers_v2_long` as a stopgap, but I’d rather fix bucketing first if it’s wrong.

Sana Farid: quick numbers from honeycomb:
- A10 decode p95 (selector=v2, longctx) +23%
- same cohort after filtering kernel_choice_id=attn_flash_v3_long: +27%
- A10 decode p95 (selector=v2, medctx): ~flat
So it’s concentrated in that long kernel choice.

Grace Kim: two actions:
1) fix bucket boundary (likely)
2) consider A10-specific kernel mapping for true longctx

Omar El-Sayed: I have a draft PR up with the boundary fix + unit tests. Would love eyes. https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/18571 (WIP) — changes decode bucket logic to treat upper bound exclusive + aligns with scheduler’s +1.

Lena Fischer: looking now. if we do upper bound exclusive, does it keep determinism? (same inputs -> same bucket)

Omar El-Sayed: yes, deterministic. basically `if effective_ctx < 4096 -> med else long` instead of `<=`. plus comments about scheduler +1.

Grace Kim: :thumbsup: can we also add a debug log (sampling) when bucket flips at boundary? (but careful on volume)

Allison Grant: sampling ok if it’s existing log stream + rate-limited. no new high-card labels.

Marcus Reed: I can run benchmark-lab A10 sweep once PR branch is built. If it fixes the classification, we should see kernel_choice shift back to med kernel for 4k-ish requests.

Connor O'Brien: what’s the rollout plan? SRE will ask if we need to rollback the canary before waiting for fix.

Sana Farid: given it’s only 5% canary, I’d prefer we keep it but add an override to force v1 on A10 long bucket if p95 keeps burning. we’re ~30 min into the alert.

Grace Kim: agree. Connor: hold the stage at 5% (no expansion). If alert persists > 45 min, we flip config to disable v2 for A10 (or force safe kernel set). Omar, can you prep the config patch?

Omar El-Sayed: yep. I can add a temporary override in the canary config: `selector_v2_enabled=false` for gpu=A10 in us-east, or more narrowly pin kernel for long bucket. Which do we prefer?

Yuki Sato: safest is disable v2 for A10 for now. pinning kernel is riskier unless we’re confident in correctness.

Grace Kim: disable v2 for A10 (us-east) as mitigation if needed. Meanwhile, merge boundary fix once tests + bench pass.

Marcus Reed: starting bench now on PR branch. Will report deltas.

Lena Fischer: reviewed PR 18571. logic looks right. one nit: add comment that scheduler adds +1 so future refactors don’t “fix” it back.

Omar El-Sayed: added comment + test case for prompt_len=4095 generating first decode token.

Sana Farid: alert is still firing but slope is flattening (traffic mix changed). I’ll keep watching the dashboard. https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/runtime-serving/latency?var-gpu=A10&var-selector=v2&from=now-2h&to=now

Marcus Reed: bench results (A10): bucket classification fixed. For mixed_long dist, p95 decode is back within +3% of v1 (was +22%). kernel_choice shifts from `attn_flash_v3_long` to `attn_flash_v3_med` for the 4k cluster.

Grace Kim: perfect. Let’s get PR 18571 landed ASAP and then re-evaluate if true longctx (8k+) on A10 still prefers different kernel.

Yuki Sato: agreed. After merge, I’ll do a focused A10 sweep at 8k/16k to see if `attn_flash_v3_long` is genuinely worse and we need an A10 override row in the registry.

Connor O'Brien: ok, I’ll note: no rollout expansion, waiting for fix. If we get another sustained breach we’ll disable v2 for A10 in canary.

Grace Kim: thanks all. Omar, ping when merged + when canary build is cut so Sana can compare pre/post.

Omar El-Sayed: will do. merging once CI green.

Sana Farid: I’ll annotate the dashboard with “bucket boundary bug suspected” + link PR so we have paper trail.
